title: sign() wraps content_mime in extra CRLF; verify() would receive different bytes than signed
description: sign.rs lines 176-177: the first MIME part (the signed content) is written as: content_mime bytes, then an appended '\r\n'. The hash in Step 2 (line 71) is computed over content_mime alone. But RFC 5751 §3.4 requires the signed content to be the exact bytes placed in the first part of the multipart/signed message. A verifier extracting the first part will see content_mime + CRLF (or content_mime without the trailing CRLF depending on multipart boundary parsing), not content_mime alone. The existing test (test_sign_output_accepted_by_openssl) passes because openssl smime -verify strips the CRLF before the boundary before hashing — but a verifier using verify() on the extracted body_range bytes would get a digest mismatch unless they know to strip the CRLF. This is a latent correctness issue for any caller that uses mime-tree to extract the signed part and feeds it to smime-tree's verify().
close_reason: False positive: test_sign_verify_roundtrip_via_mime_tree (new) passes. mime-tree strips the CRLF before the boundary per RFC 2046 §5.1.1, so body_range correctly excludes it. sign() hashes content_mime; verify() receives the same bytes.
